description.fun: Zorua is timid, and that's why it learned to transform: it hides its true identity behind illusions of people and other Pokémon to scare off danger. It often takes the shape of a silent child to go into town for food, so if a chatty child suddenly goes quiet, it may have been replaced by a Zorua. An unpractised one can leave its tail showing, just like the shape-shifting kitsune of Japanese folklore.
description.guide: Zorua is a Dark-type fox Pokémon that can disguise itself as people and other Pokémon with illusions. It is timid and mischievous, and often takes the form of a child. It evolves into Zoroark; in Hisui it has a Normal- and Ghost-type regional form.
description.tagline: A timid fox kit that hides behind illusions.

description.fun: A departed Zorua's soul, returned to life in Hisui after its kind were driven from other lands and could not survive the harsh cold. It draws power from resentment, which rises from its head as ghostly energy, and it may appear to a lone traveller wearing their own face. No other line shares its Normal and Ghost typing.

Zoroark can fool hundreds of people at once with illusions indistinguishable from reality, and it hides its den behind illusory scenery so people wander lost in the woods. Stories say those who tried to catch one were trapped in an illusion and punished. It's fiercely protective of its pack and carries its young Zorua in its mane. Ken Sugimori says that ponytail of a mane stands in for the tail it lacks.
description.guide: Zoroark is the evolved form of Zorua, a Dark-type fox Pokémon that can cast illusions powerful enough to deceive many people at once. It is deeply loyal to its pack. In Hisui it has a Normal- and Ghost-type regional form, Hisuian Zoroark.
description.tagline: A master illusionist fox that guards its pack with visions.

description.fun: With its dishevelled white mane, it looks like an embodiment of death, reborn in Hisui through spite. Its illusions are so full of malice that they can cause real harm, and it attacks so recklessly that its bitter energy cuts into its own body, yet it's devoted to those it trusts.
